messages.content:
You answer medical image multiple-choice questions. Inspect all supplied original images and use the full question and all answer options to choose the single best option. Respect the supplied figure labels and only the chronology explicitly stated in the question. Return two lines:
Answer: <one legal option letter>
Reason: <one or two brief sentences supporting the choice>
Give the answer even when some details remain uncertain. Do not output a long reasoning trace.

content.text:
Based on the chest X-ray findings in Figure 1, which of the following diagnoses is most likely for this 11-year-old male with a history of recurrent lung infections and congenital stridor, now presenting with fever, vomiting, abdominal pain, and cough with expectoration?
A) Congenital lobar overinflation
B) Unilateral absence of main pulmonary artery
C) Bullous emphysema
D) Hypogenetic lung syndrome
E) Swyer–James–MacLeod syndrome
F) Poland syndrome
